name: Old Septimus
greeting: Your uncle laid my first floor fifty years ago. Let's see if it runs in the family.

arc.line: Something simple to start. A rosette, perhaps, or a star. Your uncle always began with a rosette.
arc.after: Just like his. Better, maybe. Don't tell him I said so, wherever he is.

name: Widow Cornelia
greeting: Thieves, everywhere! I want every one of them to know there's a dog in this house. There is no dog. That's the point.

arc.line: A guard dog by the door, please, and big. Bigger than that.
arc.after: Not one thief since! Mind you, there wasn't one before either.

arc.line: The dog worked so well I want the words too. CAVE CANEM, large, so even the stupid ones understand.
arc.after: My neighbour asked to borrow the dog. I said it was busy.

arc.line: I've taken in a lodger. A cat. I'd like something pretty for the bedroom.
arc.after: The cat sleeps on it every afternoon. High praise.

name: Felix the baker
greeting: Bread is life, and the floor is where people stand while they buy it.

arc.line: Rufus opened a bakery across the road. Across the road! I want loaves on my floor, so everyone knows who bakes the real bread.
arc.after: Rufus came in to look at it. He bought a loaf. Victory.

arc.line: Rufus has copied my floor. Badly. I need a bigger one, with more on it.
arc.after: People queue just to stand on it. Some even buy bread.

arc.line: Rufus and I have made peace. We're opening a dining room together. Make it a feast.
arc.after: Nobody argues over a floor like this. Well, nobody but us.

name: Marcus the veteran
greeting: Twenty years in the legions. I like things straight, square and finished on time.

arc.line: Straight lines and a good border. Nothing that wiggles.
arc.after: Neat as a camp. Good work, soldier.

arc.line: My grandson thinks I've never seen a lion. Put one on the floor, so I can point at it while I tell him.
arc.after: He believes me now. Mostly.

name: Gaius of the baths
greeting: People come to my baths to forget the dust of the road. The floor should feel like the sea.

arc.line: An octopus. People love an octopus. Don't ask me why.
arc.after: Children try to pick it up off the floor. Business has never been better.

arc.line: The new fountain house needs glass that glitters like water.
arc.after: It sparkles even on a grey day. You are an artist, my friend.

name: Livia
greeting: I'm getting married in the spring, and everything has to be perfect. Everything.

arc.line: Doves, for love. Two of them, if you can. Facing each other.
arc.after: Mother cried. Then she asked who made it.

arc.line: We have a house now, with an atrium. Flowers, and something for good luck.
arc.after: We've had guests every day since. I may need more chairs.

name: Aulus the innkeeper
greeting: The floor of a tavern sees a lot of wine. Some of it even goes in cups.

arc.line: Amphorae. Wine jars. So the customers remember why they came.
arc.after: They keep ordering what's on the floor. Very good for trade.

arc.line: Race day is coming. Give me horses, so the gamblers feel lucky.
arc.after: Everyone lost their bets and blamed the horses. They all came back the next day.

name: Trimalchio
greeting: I have more money than the gods, and better taste. Mostly more money.

arc.line: My guests should look down and see a feast. Fish, loaves, wine. They'll be hungry before the food arrives.
arc.after: A senator laughed so hard he fell off his couch. Perfect.

arc.line: Gold. More gold. And Medusa, to frighten my brother-in-law.
arc.after: He hasn't visited since. Worth every denarius.

name: Valeria
greeting: Venus was born from the sea foam. Her house should remember it.

arc.line: Shells, for the goddess. And a border like waves.
arc.after: Pilgrims leave flowers on it. It is a good sign.

arc.line: The new temple hall is finished. It needs the finest floor in the province.
arc.after: The whole town came to the dedication. Many of them asked for you by name.

name: Quintus the aedile
trade: the magistrate in charge of public works
greeting: The town council has money to spend, and I have to spend it on something people will notice.

arc.line: The garden walk by the council house. Something dignified. Something that says the council is wise.
arc.after: Two councillors stopped arguing to admire it. A first.

arc.line: Under the old forum we've found a floor bigger than any in the province. The whole town is talking. Will you bring it back?
arc.after: The town held a festival on your floor. Your uncle's name was spoken, and yours after it. Whatever you lay next, they'll come to see it.
